idea-plugin.name: FlatBuffers Format
idea-plugin.description:
Syntax highlighting and code formatting for FlatBuffers (.fbs) schema files. Formatting runs through the platform's own formatting service, so Reformat Code (Ctrl/⌘+Alt+L) works, and enabling Settings → Tools → Actions on Save → Reformat code gives you format-on-save with no extra plugin. The formatter delegates to the flatbuffers-format CLI for byte-for-byte parity with the published engine — same output you'd get from the VS Code extension, Prettier plugin, npx flatbuffers-format, or the pre-commit hook.

Features

  • Recognises .fbs as the FlatBuffers language.
  • Syntax highlighting (keywords, types, attributes, numbers, strings, comments) via a hand-rolled lexer mirroring the engine grammar.
  • Format the current file with Ctrl/⌘ + Alt + L (the usual Reformat Code shortcut) — shells out to flatbuffers-format asynchronously.
  • Settings page at Preferences → Tools → FlatBuffers for engine discovery and every format option the engine exposes.

Prerequisites

None, on a machine with Node 20+: the plugin ships the formatter as a JavaScript bundle and runs it on the Node you already have — including one installed by nvm, fnm, Volta, asdf, nodenv or mise, which an IDE launched from the Dock or a desktop shortcut cannot see on its own PATH. Otherwise:

  • Click "Download bundled engine" on the settings page (Preferences → Tools → FlatBuffers). The plugin fetches the matching native binary from the engine's GitHub Release and caches it under the IDE system directory. No Node, no npm required.
  • Or install via npm if you prefer to manage updates yourself: npm install -g flatbuffers-format. Auto-detected on PATH after install.

Supported IDEs

All JetBrains IDEs built on the IntelliJ Platform 2024.2 or newer: IntelliJ IDEA (Community + Ultimate), Rider, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, CLion, RustRover, RubyMine, PhpStorm, Aqua, DataGrip, DataSpell, MPS, and the Android Studio fork (2024.2-aligned).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.0

  • First public release on the JetBrains Marketplace.
  • Fixed a bug that could corrupt a schema: formatting a selection, or saving with Actions on Save → Reformat code scoped to changed lines, asked for a range but got the whole formatted file back — splicing the file into itself. Partial-range requests are now declined with an explanation; the engine formats whole schemas only.
  • The formatter now ships inside the plugin as a JavaScript bundle and runs on any Node 20+ on your machine, including one installed by nvm, fnm, Volta, asdf, nodenv or mise — which an IDE started from the Dock or a desktop shortcut could not previously find. A Node below that floor is refused rather than used, and every fallback is reported once with the action that fixes it.
  • Bundled-engine download: if the flatbuffers-format CLI isn't on your PATH, the settings page can fetch a matching prebuilt binary from the project's GitHub Release and verify it against its published SHA256 sidecar.
  • The formatter's options are now real fields on the settings page — indent width, indent with tabs, line width, single-line collapsing of small enum/union/single-field bodies, max blank lines, comment reflow and comment width — each labelled with the engine's default and validated before it is saved. They used to be reachable only by typing flags into the free-text "Extra arguments" box, where a typo did nothing and said nothing. That box stays, for options the fields don't cover; anything you leave alone is still decided by the engine, not by the plugin.
  • Removed a non-functional "Format on save" checkbox. Use Settings → Tools → Actions on Save → Reformat code, which drives this formatter through the platform's formatting service.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • .fbs file-type registration.
  • Lexer-driven syntax highlighting.
  • External formatter integration via AsyncDocumentFormattingService.
  • Settings page under Tools → FlatBuffers.
  • Line/block comment toggle support (Ctrl/⌘ + /, Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + /).
